label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 repair and eight trial days

Dana, I promised last month to report back once my writer had been through a real trial. My Stenvale Aria 3 has now survived eight days of a civil trial since its visit to Harbor Point. The repair has held up well. The telephone arrangements are another matter, and worth knowing about before you leave a machine there.

I dropped it off Monday, October 19, and picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten quoted. The estimate was $285 for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. The completed work included full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning and an update from firmware 4.0.7 to 4.2.1.

Gloria also found that the internal battery was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity. She emailed with a price of $25 for replacement, parts and labor, and said she would not proceed without my approval. I approved it, bringing the final bill to $310, which I paid by card at pickup. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. I think $310 was fair for what was done. Being asked before an extra charge was added matters to me.

The first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am comfortable saying this was a successful repair, though that is still a report on eight days, not a prediction about the next eight years. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The machine came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before, and I appreciated having something specific to keep with my equipment records.

A Stenvale Aria 2 loaner was provided, so I was not left without a writer. Unfortunately, its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria in my battery approval email. She acknowledged it when my machine was ready and said they would repair the arm. I cannot say whether that has since been done.

Communication is the weak point. Their stated phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, with no voicemail box set up, so I could not even leave a message. Gloria emailed the following day about the battery, but that does not make the phone arrangement adequate. For anyone working a Monday docket, having no staffed Monday phone hours is a real limitation. Even within the advertised hours, my call went unanswered.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back. That made drop-off and pickup straightforward for me.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with your Aria 3, particularly for the number bar problem you described. I would use her again myself. I would also settle the progress-contact arrangements in advance and check the loaner’s stand before leaving. Good repair work deserves credit; an unreliable way to reach the shop still needs fixing.
